problem_markdown: Can one choose 1975 distinct points on a unit circle so that every pairwise distance is rational? Prove the answer.
solutions_markdown:
Yes. Choose 1975 distinct rational numbers $t\in(0,1)$ and define
$$u_t=\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2},\qquad v_t=\frac{2t}{1+t^2},\qquad P_t=(u_t^2-v_t^2,2u_tv_t).$$
Since $u_t^2+v_t^2=1$, each $P_t$ lies on the unit circle. The first-quadrant angles of $(u_t,v_t)$ are distinct and their doubles lie in $(0,\pi)$, so the $P_t$ are distinct. If these angles are $\theta_s,\theta_t$, their chord distance is
$$|P_sP_t|=2|\sin(\theta_s-\theta_t)|=2|v_su_t-u_sv_t|,$$
which is rational.
